stemMd: An argument claims that a park’s new signs reduced litter: litter counts fell after signs were installed. Column "alternative": select the fact that supplies a rival explanation. Column "test": select the additional evidence that best separates the signs’ effect from that rival explanation.
instructionsMd: Select exactly one answer in each named column. Both selections must be correct. The project presents separate column lists rather than the official interface’s shared matrix or drop-down controls.

options.label: A
options.textMd: alternative: The signs are made of wood

options.label: B
options.textMd: alternative: The signs describe littering rules

options.label: C
options.textMd: alternative: The park has three entrances

options.label: D
options.textMd: alternative: A cleaning crew doubled its park visits in the same week

options.label: A
options.textMd: test: Count how many signs were installed

options.label: B
options.textMd: test: Ask whether the signs are attractive

options.label: D
options.textMd: test: Compare similar parks with unchanged cleaning schedules, some receiving signs and others not

explanationMd: More frequent cleaning could reduce measured litter without signs changing behaviour. A comparison that holds cleaning schedules constant while varying signs can help isolate the effect of signs, assuming the parks are otherwise comparable.

distractorRationale.alternative-a: Material does not explain the fall in litter.
distractorRationale.alternative-c: An unchanged feature does not explain the change.
distractorRationale.test-a: Treatment count alone cannot separate cleaning effects.
distractorRationale.test-b: Attractiveness does not isolate effects on litter.
distractorRationale.test-c: The name supplies no discriminating evidence.
